before_board.S: A Kakeya set K in F_q^n.

bound_then: TWO REGIMES, neither dominating: |K| >~ q^{(n+2)/2} (best known for n < 14) and |K| >~ q^{4n/7} (better only for n >= 15). See bound_regimes.
leak: Cauchy-Schwarz sees pairwise line interactions only, which caps the exponent near n/2.

sources_before.debt: the seed wrote about q^{4n/7} with low confidence; not fetched

bound_regimes.valid_range: exceeds Wolff only for n >= 15; the two are equal at n = 14

leaks.evidence: The bush argument double-counts incidences and uses no structure in the direction set; Cauchy-Schwarz sees pairwise line interactions only.
leaks.ranking: leading for this regime (blind encoder, L2)

leaks.evidence: Bourgain-Katz-Tao supplies only a qualitative sum-product exponent, so the gain is not quantitative.
leaks.ranking: leading for this regime (blind encoder, L2)

correction.was: |K| >~ q^{(n+2)/2}, later about q^{4n/7} — ordered as though 4n/7 superseded Wolff
correction.why: (n+2)/2 > 4n/7 exactly when n < 14; they meet at n = 14. No single exponent dominated uniformly at the 2008 cutoff. The two regimes leak differently, so a single-regime bound field forced a single leak where there are two.
